en: The Scripture on the Divine Incantation of the Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yaśogupta of India during the Zhou dynasty of the Yuwen clan.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
He was surrounded before and behind by a great assembly of immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara was accompanied by countless sages and deities who maintain mantras.
Surrounded by their retinues, they approached the place where the Buddha was.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s presence, they prostrated themselves on the ground with their five limbs touching it to worship the Buddha’s feet.
After worshipping the Buddha’s feet, they circumambulated him three times and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I have a heart-mantra named 'Eleven Faces,' which was spoken by eleven hundred million Buddhas."
I now speak this for the sake of all sentient beings;
desiring to cause all sentient beings to mindfully attend to wholesome dharmas,
and desiring to cause all sentient beings to be free from sorrow and affliction.
It is for the sake of removing all illnesses of sentient beings;
for the sake of eliminating all obstacles, difficulties, calamities, portents, and evil dreams;
and for the sake of removing all untimely deaths and illnesses.
It is for the sake of making those who wish to eliminate all evil thoughts pliant and gentle;
and for the sake of ensuring that no obstacles or hindrances arise from any demons, spirits, or deities.
World-Honored One, I have never seen anyone—whether among the devas, māras, Brahmās, Śakras, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas—who [could do so].
Should there be anyone capable of receiving and upholding such a mantra—
whether by reading, reciting, copying, or disseminating it—
or who uses this mantra to protect their own body.
Alternatively, one may consecrate water with this mantra to bathe the body;
or when entering battle, or when struck by poison,
by reciting this mantra, no calamities whatsoever shall be able to prevail.
Only the calamities of past karma cannot be eliminated.
This mantra is that which all Buddhas keep in mind;
this mantra of mine is that which all Buddhas have spoken.
“World-Honored One, I recall that beyond kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
there was a Buddha named Śatapatranetra-mūrdha-anāvaraṇa-guṇaprabhāsa-rāja Tathāgata.”
At that time, I was in the presence of that Buddha as a great king among the mantra-holding rishis; it was there,
in the presence of that Buddha, that I first obtained this spell.
When one obtains this mantra, all the Buddhas of the ten directions appear before one's eyes.
Having beheld the Buddhas, one suddenly attains the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
One should know that this mantra possesses such supernatural power.
It can also benefit immeasurable sentient beings. Therefore,
you should know that good sons and good daughters who are able to read and recite it with diligent devotion day and night, without allowing it to be forgotten, [will attain great merit].
When reciting this mantra, do not allow for any other distractions.
In the early morning, bathe your body;
if you do not bathe, you should at least rinse your mouth and wash your hands.
Recite and uphold this mantra one hundred and eight times.
One who upholds this mantra shall immediately attain ten kinds of retributive fruits in their present body. What are these ten?
First, their bodies shall always be free from illness.
Second, they shall constantly be remembered by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Third, all their wealth, clothing, food, and drink [shall be abundant].
They will naturally be fully satisfied and never lack anything.
Fourth, they will be able to defeat all enemies.
Fifth, they will be able to cause all sentient beings to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness.
Sixth, no malevolent poisons or all manner of febrile diseases shall be able to inflict harm.
Seventh, no weapons or staves shall be able to cause injury.
Eighth, no water-related perils shall be able to drown or sweep them away.
Ninth, one cannot be burned by any fire-related calamities.
Tenth, one does not undergo any untimely death.
These are called the ten.
Manifesting in this body, one further attains four kinds of karmic fruition. What are these four?
First, at the time of death, one shall behold the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
Second, they shall never fall into hell;
third, they shall not be harmed by any birds or beasts;
fourth, after the end of their lives, they shall be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life.
World-Honored One, I recall that beyond kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
further beyond kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
and further beyond immeasurable kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
At that time, there was a Buddha named Mandāravagandha Tathāgata.
I was a lay follower (upāsaka) under that Buddha,
and from him I further obtained this dhāraṇī.
Having obtained this mantra, one transcends the boundaries of birth and death for forty thousand kalpas.
When this mantra is spoken, one attains the Dharma-gate of the treasury of wisdom of all Buddhas—great kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity.
By the power of this Dharma gate,
one is able to rescue all sentient beings who are imprisoned and confined within any jail.
Whether they face the execution of punishments such as cangues, shackles, stocks,
and fetters, or the various afflictions of perils such as water and fire,
I shall constantly protect them and cause them to attain liberation.
By the power of this mantra, all the yakṣas and rākṣasas were caused to give rise to wholesome minds and become fully endowed with merit;
they immediately conceived the aspiration for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This divine mantra of mine possesses such power that even if there were someone who has committed the four pārājika offenses or the five heinous crimes,
should they be able to recite this mantra once, [they would be purified].
All fundamental grave offenses shall be completely eradicated.
Such are the merits for one who recites this mantra;
how much more so for those who, relying on the teachings of this sutra, receive and uphold it.
You should know that such a person has heard this Dharma in the presence of tens of billions of nayutas of nayutas of Buddhas in the past,
and now hears it once again; how much more so for one who receives,
maintains, reads, and recites it, never forgetting it day or night.
If this person has a wish in their mind, I shall fulfill it. Furthermore,
if there is another person who, on the morning of the fourteenth or fifteenth day,
bathes their body with fragrant water and puts on new, clean clothes.
One may go to the latrine once and bathe once;
however, one must not use these purified garments while at the latrine.
When practicing this method, one shall not eat for the entire day until the following morning.
Within that place of practice, one should set up an image of Avalokiteśvara and offer various colored banners, canopies, incense, and flowers as offerings.
When first entering the place of practice,
one must be reverent and single-mindedly sincere.
All the Buddhas of the ten directions earnestly perform repentance.
Having completed the repentance, they stand before the image,
spread out a single sitting mat, kneel with their right knees on the ground, and pay homage with reverence.
Recite and uphold this mantra with a sincere heart.
One who practices this dharma should know that such a person will attain liberation from the bounds of birth and death for forty thousand kalpas.
“World-Honored One, the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is difficult to hear.
If there were someone who recited the names of a hundred thousand koṭis of Buddhas,
and another person who recited the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...”
The merit of those two persons is exactly equal and without distinction.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,"
If good sons, good daughters, and all sentient beings diligently invoke my name day and night,
they shall all attain the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*).
In this very life, one shall be freed from all suffering and affliction,
all obstacles and difficulties, and all fears; furthermore,
the transgressions of the three karmas shall all be eliminated and extinguished.
How much more so for those who, relying on the teachings of this sutra, practice according to the Dharma;
you should know that such persons will attain the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* as if it were held in the palm of their hand.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are indeed able to give rise to a mind of great loving-kindness and great compassion toward all sentient beings."
"Good sons, you should know that by means of this spiritual power,
you shall rescue and protect all sentient beings;
you will certainly achieve the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*— of this there is no doubt."
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying: "Good son, this divine mantra is also upheld by me and is also approved by me.
Good son, you should now recite it."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms.
Prostrating with his five limbs touching the ground, he paid homage at the Buddha’s feet.
Having paid homage at the Buddha’s feet, he sat to one side and addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One.”
I shall now, relying on the Buddha’s supernatural power, recite the mantra:
Namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya.
Namo saṃghāya. Namo jñānasāgaravairocanāya.
Tathāgatāya namo ārya-vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitāyai.
Bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya.
Namo sarvatathāgatavidyārājñe arhate samyaksaṃbuddhavidyārājñe.
Tadyathā | oṃ dhara dhara dhiri dhiri douru douru |
Ekajñānavijñānacchedinī (The One Who Cuts Through with Single Knowledge)
Cchā-li-pa-cchā-li-pa-cchā-li.
Kau-sū-mai kau-sū-mo-pa-li i-li mi-li chi-ti shé-luo-mo-po-na-ye.
Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇika
*Svāhā*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī possesses such supernatural power that it is the most preeminent."
Furthermore, he spoke this mantra:

*Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Tadyathā: ha ha ha ha. E le mile le ji le vi le kṣe le he le. Svāhā.* At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, this mantra is called the 'Mantra for Water' and the 'Mantra for Robes.'"
Furthermore, if there is anyone who enters the maṇḍala,
they should first recite this mantra over water seven times to bathe their body.
Having bathed their body, they should again [use] this mantra.
Recite the mantra over the robe seven times and enter the maṇḍala wearing it.
*Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya. Tadyathā: cūḷe cūḷe hā hā hā hā svāhā.* This is called the "Incense Mantra."
When first entering the *maṇḍala*, recite this mantra over the incense seven times, and only then burn it:

*Namō buddhāya | Namō dharmāya | Namō saṃghāya | Namō āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | Tadyathā | siri siri diti | diti diti siri | svāhā.* This is called the mantra for flowers, the mantra for oil, and the mantra for scattering flowers before the Buddha and lighting lamps with oil.
Recite each mantra one hundred times:

*Namo buddhāya* | *Namo dharmāya* | *Namo saṃghāya* | *Namo ārya-vairocaniprabhāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya* | *Tadyathā* | *sade sade* | *sadesade* | *sūda sūda* | *svāhā*. This is called the "Mantra for Consecrating Food."
When offering food to the Buddha, all food and drink as well as various fruits should first be consecrated twenty-one times with this mantra before being presented:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | ha si dha si | hu lu hu lu jiu lu | su lu su lu | svāhā.* This is called the "Mantra for Consecrating Fire."
Use *sumana* wood to kindle the fire.
Separately, cut thirty-one pieces of *sumana* wood, each an inch long,
and mix them with curd, clarified butter, and honey.
Take pieces of *sumana* wood, smear them with curd, ghee, and honey,
recite the mantra once over each, and cast them into the fire.
Continue this process for thirty-one pieces in succession, reciting the mantra for each.
Having recited the mantra, one should then practice according to the Dharma:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | ili mili cili mili tili hili svāhā.* This mantra is called the *Sīmābandha* (Boundary-binding) mantra.
Alternatively, one may consecrate water and scatter it in the four directions;
or consecrate mustard seeds and scatter them in the four directions;
or consecrate pure ashes and scatter them in the four directions.
Recite each mantra seven times:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | ratitiriṭiṭiṭiṭi | gaccha gaccha | bhagavan āryāvalokiteśvara svāhā.* When the practice of walking the path is completed.
Recite this mantra seven times while circumambulating Avalokiteśvara.
This mantra possesses further supernatural powers:
if there is anyone afflicted by a disease of alternating chills and fever, [they shall be cured].
Whether it occurs once a day, once every two days, or once every three days,
by reciting this mantra, all such afflictions shall be entirely cured.
Even if one is struck by malevolent spirits, [it shall be so].
Or they may be struck by Hārītī,
or struck by a rākṣasī, or struck by a piśāca ghost.
Or they may be struck by a pūtana spirit;
or struck by a bhūta spirit; or suffer from carbuncles; or suffer from fistulas;
or have sores and blisters break out on their bodies; or be bitten by snakes or stung by scorpions.
For those who have been stung by any venomous insects,
one should make mud from yellow earth, recite the mantra over it seven times,
and apply it to the site of the sting; all shall be completely healed.
If one suffers from wind-related ailments, one should recite the mantra over clarified butter seven times;
by applying it to the afflicted area and ingesting it, one will immediately be cured.
Or, if one suffers from hemiplegia or obstruction of the ears and nose.
Using *agaru* (sandalwood) with sesame oil,
boil it over birch bark while reciting the mantra seven times.
Apply it to the afflicted area, and it will be immediately cured.
All diseases treated with this mantra will be completely cured.
The spiritual power of this mantra is inexhaustible to describe;
I have spoken of it briefly here in reliance upon the scriptural teachings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
if there be good sons or good daughters..."
If there are those who are able to perform the ritual according to the instructions of Avalokiteśvara,
those good sons and good daughters must fashion an image of Avalokiteśvara out of white sandalwood.
The wood must be of fine quality and solid, not withered or hollow.
It should be one foot and three inches in length and fashioned with eleven heads;
the three faces facing forward should be made in the likeness of Bodhisattvas.
The three faces on the left side are wrathful;
the three faces on the right side resemble those of bodhisattvas with canine fangs protruding upward;
and at the back is one face making a great laugh.
On the crown of his head is one face in the form of a Buddha’s face;
all these faces are turned forward and are adorned with light.
Each of the eleven faces wears a flower crown.
Within each of their flower crowns is an Amitābha Buddha.
The left hand of Avalokiteśvara holds a *kamaṇḍalu*;
from the mouth of the vessel, lotus flowers emerge.
Extending his right hand, he makes the gesture of granting fearlessness while holding a string of jeweled ornaments;
the body of the image must be carved with these ornamental necklaces.
At that time, the person, having completed this image, [proceeds as follows].
For one who seeks that which is desired in the heart,
from the first day of the month until the fifteenth, one should enter the *maṇḍala*.
When entering the *maṇḍala*, one should defecate once and bathe once.
One must possess three sets of clean robes and change them three times a day;
at the time of dawn, one puts on one set.
At midday he wears one set,
and toward evening he wears another set;
his clean robes are not worn over the upper screen.
A practitioner on the path shall observe a fast for one meal,
abstaining from all other flavors and consuming only barley milk gruel.
The place where the altar of practice is established must be a clean chamber.
Wipe it clean with clay and smear the ground with fragrant mud;
then sprinkle the ground with scented water.
Within that chamber, measure out a space of seven cubits, equal in length and breadth.
At the four corners, erect pillars and hang banners all around.
In the center, arrange a high seat upon which place an image of Avalokiteśvara, facing west.
He scattered various kinds of flowers upon his site of enlightenment and burned only aloeswood, storax,
and other such incenses for seven days, from the first day until the seventh.
Recite the mantra three times each day:
one hundred and eight times in the morning,
and one hundred and eight times at midday.
Recite one hundred and eight times toward evening;
there is no need yet to offer food.
This continues from the eighth day at midday until the thirteenth day.
Every day, one should offer various kinds of food and drink, as well as other fruits.
The food offered should not be placed upon a plate;
rather, one should simply spread clean grass and set the food and drink upon it.
On the fourteenth and fifteenth days,
one should redouble the offerings of exquisite incense and flowers,
as well as various delicacies and assorted fruits.
Doubly superior to what was previously offered, these were presented to the Buddha.
As for the practitioner, they simply spread *śāla* grass as a seat,
kneeling on their right knees with reverence, facing directly toward the image.
On the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the lunar month,
one should kindle a sandalwood fire before the image;
one *śrona* of *sumana* oil should be placed in a clean copper vessel.
Place it before the practitioner.
Furthermore, one must prepare agallochum incense, with pieces as thick as a sinew,
cut into one thousand and eight segments, each an inch long.
At that time, from the latter part of the fifteenth day,
the practitioner takes a piece of agalloch wood,
anoints it with *soma* oil, and recites the mantra over it once.
He cast them into the sandalwood fire,
continuing in this manner until all one thousand and eight pieces were exhausted.
At that time, the practitioner did not consume any food at all for two full days.
On the night of the fifteenth day,
Avalokiteśvara came into the ritual arena;
the sandalwood image moved of its own accord.
When the image moves, the trichiliocosm shakes simultaneously.
From the face of the Buddha atop the image’s head, a voice issues forth, praising the practitioner and saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family! I have come to see you."
All aspirations have now been completely fulfilled.
At that time, there were four aspirations; what are these four?
First, the aspiration not to leave one's seat.
First, one immediately attains the power to soar through the air, moving with sovereign ease and without obstruction.
Second, one vows to attain non-obstruction among all worthy sages and saints.
Third, one vows to become a king among the rishis who uphold mantras.
Fourth, one vows that upon manifesting the body, one shall immediately follow after Avalokiteśvara.
These are called the four vows.
At that time, the practitioner may request whatever they desire from among these four vows.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara granted him one vow.
Among those four vows, if it should become unavoidable,
he was to establish the *dharmāyatana* (sacred site) again at dawn on the fifteenth day of the following month.
Within the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), place one image;
if it contains śarīra relics,
it should be an image of the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara.
Place the śarīra relics beside the image.
One requires one thousand and eight stalks of flowers.
The practitioner, before the image, spreads grass for a seat and kneels in the *hu-kuei* (half-lotus) posture with reverence.
Take one flower, recite the mantra over it once, and scatter it upon the image.
Proceed in this manner in succession until all one thousand and eight flowers have been exhausted.
When the flowers are finished:
At that time, from the face of the Bodhisattva directly before the image of Avalokiteśvara, a great peal of thunder issues forth.
At that moment, the practitioner should settle the mind and fix the intent, remaining free from fear.
When the thunder resounds, all things tremble.
At that time, the practitioner should constantly recite mantras with their mouth.
When the sound of thunder emerges, they should immediately make a request and raise their voice, chanting:
"Namo Avalokiteśvara."
"Disciple, when will you be able to rescue all sentient beings from their suffering and affliction?
When will you be able to fulfill the aspirations of all sentient beings?
At that time, Avalokiteśvara granted them immediately according to their wishes.
When making this vow,
the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, and all spirits will be unable to create obstacles or difficulties.
If one uses a copper bowl during a lunar eclipse, [one should perform the rite].
Place three *liǎng* of cow ghee and,
at that spot along the road in front of the image of Avalokiteśvara,
smear the ground with yellow clay.
The ball should be one chi and five cun in diameter.
Place a butter bowl upon it and recite the mantra starting from the moment of the first eclipse.
This continues until the moon returns to its original state,
after which one finally ceases [the practice].
One should take the clarified butter (*sarpis*) for consumption and eat it until it is entirely exhausted.
One must not leave any remainder.
Having consumed this ghee, all diseases within the body will be completely cured.
Use realgar, orpiment, and yellow arsenic.
Place two portions of equal measure upon blades of grass before an image of Avalokiteśvara,
and recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Having performed the incantation, one should bathe the body with that water mixed with warm water;
all obstacles, all evil dreams,
and all epidemics shall be entirely cured and eliminated.
If enemies or bandits from other regions should wish to invade the borders,
one should face this image of Avalokiteśvara directly toward them and make offerings with various kinds of incense and flowers.
Take a portion of soot the size of a soybean;
recite the mantra one thousand and eight times,
and smear it on the wrathful face on the left side of the image.
It shall cause those enemies to be unable to advance.
Should an epidemic arise among the people of a land,
or should a pestilential death afflict various kinds of domestic animals, [this shall likewise prevail].
Establish the site of practice (*maṇḍala*).
Use white mustard seeds to press out the oil until one *śeṣa* (one *liang*) is obtained.
Take wood from the purple *kāśmarya* tree, as thick as a writing brush handle.
Cut it into exactly one thousand and eight pieces.
First, burn purple acacia wood before the image;
the person takes one piece of the purple acacia.
Recite the mantra once over white mustard seed oil and cast it into the fire for as many portions as there are;
having recited the mantra once over each portion, cast them all into the fire.
It can cause all pestilential diseases to be completely cured and healed.
If there is anyone who has fallen ill due to being subjected to malevolent incantations, sorcery,
or curses, such a person should remain before the image.
Using crimson thread, recite the mantra once for each knot;
after reciting it seven times, form seven knots.
Tie them to the crown of the image's head and leave it there for one night.
If one takes [this] and ties it around the neck of a sick person, they will immediately be cured.
If someone suddenly contracts a case of madness,
one should use white thread to tie twenty-one knots.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Then, before the image, recite it one hundred and eight more times.
Bind [the thread] to the very top of the head on the front of this image.
Go directly and fasten it around the neck of the patient for one night.
If they have not recovered after two days have passed,
return and take the mantra-cord, reciting the mantra over it one hundred and eight times once more.
If one ties it around the neck of an image and leaves it for another night,
then taking it to bind the patient will result in immediate recovery. Furthermore,
if there are malevolent spirits who have entered a person's house...
One hundred and eight grains of frankincense should be placed before the image;
reciting the mantra once over each grain, they should be cast into the fire.
Once this incense is exhausted, all malevolent spirits [will be subdued].
They will naturally disperse and flee, not daring to remain stationary.
If there are enemies or仇讎 (enemies) who watch for an opportunity to harm one,
[one should take] white thread and place it before the image.
Tie one hundred and eight knots and recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times.
Fasten them to the top of the head on the left side of the image facing the wrathful direction, and leave it there for one night.
Take hold of this cord and call out the names of those enemies;
with each utterance, cut one knot until all one hundred and eight knots are exhausted.
If you constantly call out the names of these people, what you do will not succeed.

If there are those who harbor mutual resentment or hatred toward one another, they should take five-colored threads and fashion a mantra-cord; reciting the mantra before the image, they shall tie it upon the crown of the head of the one facing the left side of the shrine.
After remaining for a single night, they may untie and take it away, and their [enmity] will be greatly increased [in its resolution].
It causes those who are angry to naturally reach a reconciliation.
If anyone wishes to seek auspicious matters,
they should take five-colored threads and tie them into a mantra-cord.
Recite the mantra seven times before the image.
Fasten it to the crown of one's head directly in front for one night.
Upon removing it, whatever one seeks shall be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
If there is anyone who knows that there are obstacles or difficulties within their own body,
they must apply various blended incenses to the body of the image and further bathe the image with scented water.
Having bathed the image, take this water back and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times while bathing your own body.
Once you have bathed your body, all obstacles and difficulties will naturally be extinguished.
When this chapter was being spoken, the entire great assembly simultaneously praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Great Being Avalokiteśvara!
You are indeed able to protect all sentient beings by proclaiming this great divine mantra."
"We, the great assembly, shall likewise uphold it.
Having spoken this sutra, that great assembly rose simultaneously,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, paid homage, and departed.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-ekādaśamukha-avalokiteśvara-vidyārāja-sūtra* is also known as the *Vajramahāmaṇḍala-vidyārāja-sūtra*.
It consists of one hundred thousand verses in its full collection;
this [text] is an abbreviated excerpt consisting of the single chapter on the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara.
